Hi Tara — thanks for the context and the export — that spike makes sense given the new ingest. Two pragmatic options we typically offer (ballpark numbers below; see attached short proposal):

Option A — Top-up (prorated, fastest)
- Add a temporary committed bucket for the remainder of the current term (prorated to 12/15/2026).
- Unit price is based on current tier; we can offer a 10% uplift discount on the incremental units for the prorated period.
- Billing: pro-rated invoice or credit voucher per your preference.
- Pros: minimal legal; procurement can approve a PO quickly; live in 3–5 business days.

Option B — Annualize-now + co-term (preferred for predictability)
- Move to an elevated annual commitment now and align the renewal to 12/15/2026 (co-term).
- We'll amortize the remainder of the pro-rated period into the new commitment.
- Discount range: 12–15% on unit price depending on final committed annual run-rate.
- Requires a short amendment (legal) and PO; timeline ~7–10 business days to sign and provision.

Ballpark example using your Q2 delta: incremental 8M tokens/month -> Option A incremental cost ~= $7.2k (after 10% uplift discount prorated); Option B annualized (12% discount assumed) ~= $68k for the remaining contract window + rebase going into next year (sample calc attached).

Next steps I recommend: confirm the delta you want to cover (e.g., 8M tokens/month) and whether procurement prefers invoice vs voucher. I've attached a 1-pager summary (RIUplift_Proposal_Summary.pdf) — if you confirm numbers I can get internal approvals and return a redlined amendment or PO invoice.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
